nodes.title: SG-5.1 · Single content-driven runner
nodes.body:
Context: game/src/systems holds conditions.ts, dialogue.ts, events.ts, inventory.ts and interaction.ts. game/src/engine/scene.ts has performAction and dialogue.ts has chooseOption, each as separate entry points with no emitted-event output. Desired behavior: one runner module takes (content, state, input) and returns new state plus the emitted events, driven only by the scene content. Expected result: game/src/systems/runner.ts is pure, has no Phaser or React dependency, and is covered by unit tests on fixture content. Why: it is the single path SG-5.2 will route the running game through.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given content, a state and an action input, when runStep is called, then it returns { state, events } where state is a new object and events lists the applied GameEvents in order
- Given a choose input for the active dialogue node, when runStep is called, then choice events are applied, the choice text is added to history and activeDialogue becomes choice.next or null
- Given an action whose conditions fail, an unknown object, action or choice index, when runStep is called, then the same state object is returned with an empty events array
- Given the runner source, then it imports nothing from phaser, react, or game/frontend, does not mutate its inputs and is under 200 lines
- Given fixture content in game/tests/fixtures, when the runner tests run with npm test in game/, then they pass without Phaser or React


## Scope
- In scope: game/src/systems/runner.ts
- In scope: game/tests/runner.test.ts with fixture content
- Out of scope: Routing useGame/App through the runner and removing performAction/chooseOption (SG-5.2)
- Out of scope: New content, features or UI changes
- Out of scope: backend/
- Preserve: Existing performAction, chooseOption and their tests
- Preserve: Phaser pinned at ~3.90.0 and the phaser-pin guard test
- Preserve: Zustand store as the only owner of GameState
- Preserve: Gameplay of the boys-room world


## Technical constraints
- Phaser stays pinned at ~3.90.0
- No source file in game/src over 200 lines
- game/src never imports from game/frontend
- npm test and npm run typecheck pass in game/ and game/frontend/
- No test deleted or skipped; tests mock only what is external


## Definition of done
- runner.ts exists and is pure
- Runner unit tests pass; typecheck passes in game/ and game/frontend/


## Non-functional requirements
- No per-call allocations beyond the new state and events array


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Runner applies object actions through conditions and events and reports emitted events
nodes.body:
Context: performAction in game/src/engine/scene.ts evaluates action.conditions with evaluateAll then applyEvents, but returns only state. Desired behavior: runStep(content, state, {type:'action', objectId, actionId}) does the same purely and also returns the applied events. Expected result: item pickup, flag and scene changes come out as state plus an events list. Why: the running game needs emitted events from a single runner.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given an action with add_item and set_flag events and passing conditions, when runStep runs, then state.inventory and state.flags change on a new object and events equals the action events in order
- Given an action with a failing condition, an unknown objectId or an unknown actionId, when runStep runs, then the same state reference and [] events are returned
- Given a frozen input state, when runStep runs, then it does not throw and the input is unchanged


## Scope
- In scope: Action path of runStep
- Out of scope: Dialogue path
- Out of scope: Rewiring useGame
- Preserve: performAction behaviour


## Technical constraints
- Reuse evaluateAll from systems/conditions.ts and applyEvents from systems/events.ts
- No Phaser or React imports; file under 200 lines


## Definition of done
- Action path implemented in game/src/systems/runner.ts


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Runner advances dialogue choices over scene content
nodes.body:
Context: chooseOption in game/src/systems/dialogue.ts uses getActiveNode, applyEvents and addHistory. Desired behavior: runStep(content, state, {type:'choose', index}) resolves the active node from content.scene.dialogue, applies choice events, records the choice text and moves activeDialogue, returning emitted events. Expected result: dialogue progression runs from data through the same runner. Why: dialogue and events must share one entry point.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given activeDialogue pointing at a node and a valid index, when runStep runs, then choice events are applied, history gains the choice text and activeDialogue equals choice.next
- Given a choice without next, then activeDialogue becomes null
- Given no active dialogue or an out-of-range index, then the same state reference and [] events are returned


## Scope
- In scope: Choose path of runStep
- In scope: RunnerContent, RunnerInput and RunnerResult types
- Out of scope: Action path
- Out of scope: Rewiring App/useGame
- Preserve: chooseOption behaviour


## Technical constraints
- Reuse getActiveNode from systems/dialogue.ts and addHistory from state/gameState.ts
- No Phaser or React imports; file under 200 lines


## Definition of done
- Choose path implemented in game/src/systems/runner.ts


## Clarifying questions
- None

steps.action: Create the file and export type RunnerContent = { scene: SceneDef }; type RunnerInput = { type: 'action'; objectId: string; actionId: string } | { type: 'choose'; index: number }; type RunnerResult = { state: GameState; events: GameEvent[] }. Import SceneDef, GameState, GameEvent from '../state/types'.
steps.expected: Types compile under npm run typecheck in game/.

steps.action: Add export function runStep(content, state, input): RunnerResult. For input.type === 'action': find the object in content.scene.objects by objectId and its action by actionId (as performAction in game/src/engine/scene.ts L28-L47 does); if either is missing or evaluateAll(state, action.conditions) is false return { state, events: [] }; otherwise return { state: applyEvents(state, action.events), events: action.events }. For input.type === 'choose' return { state, events: [] } for now (filled by the REQ2 Act). Import evaluateAll from './conditions' and applyEvents from './events'.
steps.code: return { state: applyEvents(state, action.events), events: action.events };

steps.action: Replace the placeholder choose return: const node = getActiveNode(state, content.scene); const choice = node?.choices[input.index]; if (!node || !choice) return { state, events: [] }; const events = choice.events ??
